nodes.procedure: The commercial nickel foam was sonicated sequentially with acetone, ethanol, 2M HCl aqueous solution, and deionized water for 30 min, respectively.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiMoO4·nH2O synthesis
nodes.procedure: A piece of washed nickel foam (1×2 cm²) was immersed in the reaction solution of 15 mL containing Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.04 M) and (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O (0.01 M) in a Teflon autoclave. Then, the autoclave was sealed and heated in an oven at 150°C for 6 h. After washing with deionized water, the product of NiMoO4·nH2O nanoarray was obtained.

nodes.name: Phosphatization to P-NiMoO4
nodes.procedure: The obtained NiMoO4·nH2O sample was annealed at 500°C for 4 h using 1.0 g NaH2PO2·H2O as the phosphorus source to obtain phosphorus-doped nickel molybdate (P-NiMoO4) in Ar atmosphere.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH with activation (LSV cycles)
nodes.source_text: The HER electrochemical performance was evaluated in a three-electrode cell using 1M KOH solution... progressively increasing HER activity... reduced overpotential corresponding to 10mAcm⁻² from the initial 92.9mV to 48.9mV at the 1000th cycle... Tafel slopes gradually decreased... approached 46mVdec⁻¹... remained nearly unchanged for at least 120h... polarization curve after 2000 LSVs exhibited negligible change.
Clearly, the performance of P - NiMoO₄ is substantially better than that of NiMoO₄... The Tafel slope plummeted from 164mVdec⁻¹ for NiMoO₄ to 74mVdec⁻¹ for P - NiMoO₄.

nodes.description: UOR performance in 1 M KOH with 0.33 M urea
nodes.source_text: The UOR activity of P - NiMoO₄ was evaluated in 1M KOH with urea... optimized UOR activity was achieved at the urea concentration of 0.33M... needs 1.35V (versus RHE) to drive a current density of 100mA cm⁻²... Tafel slope of 19mVdec⁻¹... remained nearly unchanged after working continuously for 24h at 1.28V versus RHE.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMoO4 shows single-phase α-NiMoO4 with peaks at 14.3°, 19.1°, 25.3° etc. corresponding to monoclinic NiMoO4 (PDF#08-9796). P-NiMoO4 shows additional peaks at 26.57° and 27.19° attributed to (220) and (11-2) planes of β-NiMoO4 (PDF#45-0142).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Apparently, single-phase α-NiMoO4 without phosphorus source was formed (Figure 1b) with the peaks at 14.3°, 19.1°, 25.3°, 28.8°, 32.6°, 38.7°, 41.2°, 43.9°, 47.4°, 50.0, 54.0, 57.2, 58.3, 60.8, 62.3, and 67.0 corresponding to (110), (20-1), (20-2), (220), (022), (003), (040), (330), (20-4), (11-4), (15-1), (44-1), (402), (20-5), (152), and (134) planes of monoclinic NiMoO4 (PDF#08-9796) ... two additional diffraction peaks at 26.57° and 27.19° were observed after phosphorylation, which can be well attributed to the (220) and (11-2) planes of β-NiMoO4 (PDF#45-0142), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMoO4 shows micropillar array morphology. P-NiMoO4 preserves micropillar array but surface became rougher with more cracks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the micropillar array morphology was preserved after phosphorylation and however, the surface became rougher with apparently more cracks probably due to the stress concentration at the grain boundaries of α-NiMoO4 and β-NiMoO4 (Figure 1d,e).

nodes.characterization_summary: P-NiMoO4 shows lattice fringes of 0.618 nm and 0.335 nm assigned to (110) plane of α-NiMoO4 and (220) plane of β-NiMoO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The microscopic structure of the samples was further studied by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) (Figure 1f,g). Two regions with the lattice fringes of 0.618 and 0.335 nm were observed, which can be well assigned to the (110) plane of α-NiMoO4 and the (220) plane of β-NiMoO4.

nodes.characterization_summary: P-NiMoO4 survey spectrum confirms Ni, Mo, O, P elements. P 2p peak at ≈134 eV indicates successful P doping without phosphide formation. Ni 2p peaks at 874.4 eV (2p1/2) and 857.1 eV (2p3/2) for Ni2+, positively shifted vs NiMoO4. Mo 3d shows Mo4+ (229.1 eV), Mo5+ (230.3 eV), Mo6+ (232.3 eV). O 1s new peak at 531.2 eV assigned to oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the survey spectrum confirmed the existence of Ni, Mo, O, and P elements in P-NiMoO4. In particular, the distinct peak at ≈134 eV indicates the successful doping of phosphorus elements into NiMoO4 rather than the formation of phosphides. For Ni 2p the peaks at 874.4 and 857.1 eV can be ascribed to Ni2+ 2p1/2 and Ni2+ 2p3/2, respectively. Compared to NiMoO4, the binding energy of Ni 2p is positively shifted due to P doping ... In the region of Mo 3d, ... the peaks in P-NiMoO4 can be deconvoluted into three components of Mo4+, Mo5+, and Mo6+ with the peaks of Mo 3d5/2 at 229.1, 230.3, and 232.3 eV, respectively ... By fitting the signal, a new dominated peak at 531.2 eV assigned to oxygen vacancies (Ov) was observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: P-NiMoO4-1000 shows d-spacings of 0.618 nm (α-NiMoO4 (110)), 0.335 nm (β-NiMoO4 (220)), and 0.219 nm (Ni2P (111)). More porous and rougher surface observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, in the HRTEM image of P-NiMoO4-1000, three regions were observed (Figure 3f) and the clear d-spacing of 0.618, 0.335, and 0.219 nm can be well attributed to the (1 1 0) plane of α-NiMoO4, the (2 2 0) plane of β-NiMoO4, and the (1 1 1) plane of hexagonal Ni2P (PDF#03-0953), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: P-NiMoO4 at different activation stages: P 2p shows new peak at 129.3 eV (P-Ni bonding). Ni 2p shows Ni-P at 852.8 eV. Mo 3d and O 1s show shifts indicating changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Surprisingly, as shown in Figure 3a, a new peak at 129.3 eV attributed to the P-Ni bonding was observed in the spectrum of P 2p ... the formation of metal phosphide was further confirmed by the presence of a characteristic peak of the Ni-P bonding at 852.8 eV in the region of Ni 2p (Figure 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrolyte after 200 LSV cycles shows dissolved P, Ni, Mo with larger Mo amount. After further cycles, Ni and P constant, Mo decreases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further study the change of the surface composition of the catalyst, the elemental content of the electrolyte was monitored by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). As shown in Figure 3d, all the elements of P, Ni, and Mo in the electrocatalyst were detected in the electrolyte after 200 LSV cycles, and particularly, a larger amount of Mo was dissolved into the electrolyte than Ni and P during the first 200 LSV cycles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pre- and post-activation samples show Mo-O vibrations at 339, 809, 881, 931 cm⁻¹. New peaks at 706 and 190 cm⁻¹ after activation attributed to Mo-O-Mo in Mo₂O₇²⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To validate this hypothesis, the structural evolution during the activation of P-NiMo4 was examined by Raman spectroscopy (Figure 3e). A set of strong Raman peaks can be observed at 339, 809, 881, and 931 cm⁻¹ in both pre-and postactivation samples, which are consistent with Mo-O vibrations in NiMoO4. In contrast, the new peaks at 706 and 190 cm⁻¹ after activation are attributed to the asymmetric extension and bending modes of the Mo-O-Mo bond, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: P-NiMoO4 Cdl = 256.94 mF cm⁻², P-NiMoO4-200 Cdl = 112.04 mF cm⁻², P-NiMoO4-1000 Cdl = 139.41 mF cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Cdl dropped significantly from 256.94 mF cm⁻² of P-NiMoO4 to 112.04 mF cm⁻² of P-NiMoO4-200 and then slightly increased to 139.41 mF cm⁻² for P-NiMoO4-1000.
